title: Before and After
label: ch:ml-before-after
canDo: I can say that something happens before or after a named time or a named event.

payoff.summary: From cold: the two words that order events, and the ending they both lean on.
payoff.note: THE NOTE'S FIRST HALF IS TRUE AND ITS SECOND HALF IS NOT, AND THE DRAFT OF THIS NOTE CELEBRATED IT AS THE FIRST TRUSTWORTHY NOTE OF THE RUN. It read 'munpu and shesham are not taught' -- verifiably true, neither appears anywhere in the corpus -- and then 'pinne (then) is the nearest and it SEQUENCES TURNS RATHER THAN EVENTS'. ML-C68-at-first (2350) teaches the opposite in as many words: 'aadyaM puts an ACTION first in TIME, and it pairs with pinne', its summary table is headed 'an action in time', and its worked example is aadyaM uuNu, pinne chaaya -- lunch first, then tea, which orders the world and not the telling of it. I TOOK THE NOTE'S OWN ANTICIPATION OF THE DOMAIN CHECK AS EVIDENCE THAT THE CHECK HAD BEEN DONE. That is the domain mode one level up: not trusting a note's list of words, but trusting a note's self-assessment. FIFTH stale note in five tranches, not the first sound one. THE ORGANISING CONTRAST WAS REBUILT ON WHAT THE CORPUS ACTUALLY TEACHES. Both pairs order real events. What aadyaM and pinne cannot do is NAME what they measure against -- they lay a run out, this then that. munpu and shEshaM fix an event against a NAMED point, which is what 'anteriority and posteriority' asks for, so TIME-09 still closes, on a true framing rather than the draft's false one. THREE MORE CLAIMS WERE WRONG AND ARE FIXED: 'munpu and shEshaM cannot stand alone' is false Malayalam (shEshaM is a standalone noun, as this chapter's own lesson says when it glosses it 'the remainder'); the recall's 'neither word changed the word in front of it' contradicted the ordering lesson, since it is shEshaM that puts uuNu into the dative; and 'one ending, four jobs' counted to FIVE by its own enumeration while omitting the dative SUBJECT that ML-C06-dative-subject owns. The jobs are now named, not counted. NO NEW GRAMMAR: both words are postpositions on the dative, so raNTu maNikku munpu reuses ML-C102-manikku's form and uuNinu shEshaM shows the dative's other shape on uuNu, owned since 930. The draft presented that ending as derivable and it was not -- ML-C06 says the choice is made 'by the sound the noun ends in' and never says WHICH sounds -- so the lesson now supplies the one rule it needs: a word ending in a consonant takes -inu. shEshaM LANDS ON KNOWN SCRIPT DEBT AND NOTHING CAN BE DONE ABOUT IT HERE. U+0D36 has no script lesson (SCR-12's 'sha', re-derived in chapter 103 as 12 distinct tokens across 15 headword fields). It does not trip neverTaughtGlyphs because it sits inside other letter lessons' examples, and closure is measured in READING ORDER -- shari needs that letter in CHAPTER 1, so a lesson at 3870 retires nothing. Filed against HL-C407, and the word is not avoided for it.
